tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
2	from enum import IntEnum, unique
3	from typing import Optional, Sequence, Union
4	
5	import numpy as np
6	import torch
7	from torch import Tensor
8	
9	from .base_box3d import BaseInstance3DBoxes
10	from .cam_box3d import CameraInstance3DBoxes
11	from .depth_box3d import DepthInstance3DBoxes
12	from .lidar_box3d import LiDARInstance3DBoxes
13	from .utils import limit_period
14	
15	
16	@unique
17	class Box3DMode(IntEnum):
18	    """Enum of different ways to represent a box.
19	
20	    Coordinates in LiDAR:
21	
22	    .. code-block:: none
23	
24	                    up z
25	                       ^   x front
26	                       |  /
27	                       | /
28	        left y <------ 0
29	
30	    The relative coordinate of bottom center in a LiDAR box is (0.5, 0.5, 0),
31	    and the yaw is around the z axis, thus the rotation axis=2.
32	
33	    Coordinates in Camera:
34	
35	    .. code-block:: none
36	
37	                z front
38	               /
39	              /
40	             0 ------> x right
41	             |
42	             |
43	             v
44	        down y
45	
46	    The relative coordinate of bottom center in a CAM box is (0.5, 1.0, 0.5),
47	    and the yaw is around the y axis, thus the rotation axis=1.
48	
49	    Coordinates in Depth:
50	
51	    .. code-block:: none
52	
53	        up z
54	           ^   y front
55	           |  /
56	           | /
57	           0 ------> x right
58	
59	    The relative coordinate of bottom center in a DEPTH box is (0.5, 0.5, 0),
60	    and the yaw is around the z axis, thus the rotation axis=2.
61	    """
62	
63	    LIDAR = 0
64	    CAM = 1
65	    DEPTH = 2
66	
67	    @staticmethod
68	    def convert(
69	        box: Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor, BaseInstance3DBoxes],
70	        src: 'Box3DMode',
71	        dst: 'Box3DMode',
72	        rt_mat: Optional[Union[np.ndarray, Tensor]] = None,
73	        with_yaw: bool = True,
74	        correct_yaw: bool = False
75	    ) -> Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor, BaseInstance3DBoxes]:
76	        """Convert boxes from ``src`` mode to ``dst`` mode.
77	
78	        Args:
79	            box (Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or
80	                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`): Can be a k-tuple, k-list or an Nxk
81	                array/tensor.
82	            src (:obj:`Box3DMode`): The source box mode.
83	            dst (:obj:`Box3DMode`): The target box mode.
84	            rt_mat (np.ndarray or Tensor, optional): The rotation and
85	                translation matrix between different coordinates.
86	                Defaults to None. The conversion from ``src`` coordinates to
87	                ``dst`` coordinates usually comes along the change of sensors,
88	                e.g., from camera to LiDAR. This requires a transformation
89	                matrix.
90	            with_yaw (bool): If ``box`` is an instance of
91	                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`, whether or not it has a yaw angle.
92	                Defaults to True.
93	            correct_yaw (bool): If the yaw is rotated by rt_mat.
94	                Defaults to False.
95	
96	        Returns:
97	            Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or
98	            :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`: The converted box of the same type.
99	        """
100	        if src == dst:
101	            return box
102	
103	        is_numpy = isinstance(box, np.ndarray)
104	        is_Instance3DBoxes = isinstance(box, BaseInstance3DBoxes)
105	        single_box = isinstance(box, (list, tuple))
106	        if single_box:
107	            assert len(box) >= 7, (
108	                'Box3DMode.convert takes either a k-tuple/list or '
109	                'an Nxk array/tensor, where k >= 7')
110	            arr = torch.tensor(box)[None, :]
111	        else:
112	            # avoid modifying the input box
113	            if is_numpy:
114	                arr = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(box)).clone()
115	            elif is_Instance3DBoxes:
116	                arr = box.tensor.clone()
117	            else:
118	                arr = box.clone()
119	
120	        if is_Instance3DBoxes:
121	            with_yaw = box.with_yaw
122	
123	        # convert box from `src` mode to `dst` mode.
124	        x_size, y_size, z_size = arr[..., 3:4], arr[..., 4:5], arr[..., 5:6]
125	        if with_yaw:
126	            yaw = arr[..., 6:7]
127	        if src == Box3DMode.LIDAR and dst == Box3DMode.CAM:
128	            if rt_mat is None:
129	                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[0, -1, 0], [0, 0, -1], [1, 0, 0]])
130	            xyz_size = torch.cat([x_size, z_size, y_size], dim=-1)
131	            if with_yaw:
132	                if correct_yaw:
133	                    yaw_vector = torch.cat([
134	                        torch.cos(yaw),
135	                        torch.sin(yaw),
136	                        torch.zeros_like(yaw)
137	                    ],
138	                                           dim=1)
139	                else:
140	                    yaw = -yaw - np.pi / 2
141	                    yaw = limit_period(yaw, period=np.pi * 2)
142	        elif src == Box3DMode.CAM and dst == Box3DMode.LIDAR:
143	            if rt_mat is None:
144	                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[0, 0, 1], [-1, 0, 0], [0, -1, 0]])
145	            xyz_size = torch.cat([x_size, z_size, y_size], dim=-1)
146	            if with_yaw:
147	                if correct_yaw:
148	                    yaw_vector = torch.cat([
149	                        torch.cos(-yaw),
150	                        torch.zeros_like(yaw),
151	                        torch.sin(-yaw)
152	                    ],
153	                                           dim=1)
154	                else:
155	                    yaw = -yaw - np.pi / 2
156	                    yaw = limit_period(yaw, period=np.pi * 2)
157	        elif src == Box3DMode.DEPTH and dst == Box3DMode.CAM:
158	            if rt_mat is None:
159	                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[1, 0, 0], [0, 0, -1], [0, 1, 0]])
160	            xyz_size = torch.cat([x_size, z_size, y_size], dim=-1)
161	            if with_yaw:
162	                if correct_yaw:
163	                    yaw_vector = torch.cat([
164	                        torch.cos(yaw),
165	                        torch.sin(yaw),
166	                        torch.zeros_like(yaw)
167	                    ],
168	                                           dim=1)
169	                else:
170	                    yaw = -yaw

172	            if rt_mat is None:

186	            if rt_mat is None:

221	            rt_mat = arr.new_tensor(rt_mat)

# Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
import warnings
from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import Iterator, Optional, Sequence, Union

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import Tensor

from mmdet3d.structures.bbox_3d.utils import rotation_3d_in_axis


class BasePoints:
    """Base class for Points.

    Args:
        tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[Sequence[float]]): The points
            data with shape (N, points_dim).
        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
            is (x, y, z, ...). Defaults to 3.
        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
            extra dimension. Defaults to None.

    Attributes:
        tensor (Tensor): Float matrix with shape (N, points_dim).
        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
            is (x, y, z, ...).
        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
            extra dimension. Defaults to None.
        rotation_axis (int): Default rotation axis for points rotation.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray, Sequence[Sequence[float]]],
                 points_dim: int = 3,
                 attribute_dims: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        if isinstance(tensor, Tensor):
            device = tensor.device
        else:
            device = torch.device('cpu')
        tensor = torch.as_tensor(tensor, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        if tensor.numel() == 0:
            # Use reshape, so we don't end up creating a new tensor that does
            # not depend on the inputs (and consequently confuses jit)
            tensor = tensor.reshape((-1, points_dim))
        assert tensor.dim() == 2 and tensor.size(-1) == points_dim, \
            ('The points dimension must be 2 and the length of the last '
             f'dimension must be {points_dim}, but got points with shape '
             f'{tensor.shape}.')

        self.tensor = tensor.clone()
        self.points_dim = points_dim
        self.attribute_dims = attribute_dims
        self.rotation_axis = 0

    @property
    def coord(self) -> Tensor:
        """Tensor: Coordinates of each point in shape (N, 3)."""
        return self.tensor[:, :3]

    @coord.setter
    def coord(self, tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray]) -> None:
        """Set the coordinates of each point.

        Args:
            tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray): Coordinates of each point with shape
                (N, 3).
        """
        try:
            tensor = tensor.reshape(self.shape[0], 3)
        except (RuntimeError, ValueError):  # for torch.Tensor and np.ndarray
            raise ValueError(f'got unexpected shape {tensor.shape}')
        if not isinstance(tensor, Tensor):
            tensor = self.tensor.new_tensor(tensor)
        self.tensor[:, :3] = tensor

    @property
    def height(self) -> Union[Tensor, None]:
        """Tensor or None: Returns a vector with height of each point in shape
        (N, )."""
        if self.attribute_dims is not None and \
                'height' in self.attribute_dims.keys():
            return self.tensor[:, self.attribute_dims['height']]
        else:
            return None

    @height.setter
    def height(self, tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray]) -> None:
        """Set the height of each point.

        Args:

137	
138	### KITTI
139	
140	The raw annotation of KITTI is under camera coordinate system, see [get_label_anno](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/tools/dataset_converters/kitti_data_utils.py). For training vision-based models, the data is kept in the camera coordinate system.
141	
142	In SECOND, the LiDAR coordinate system for a box is defined as follows (a bird's eye view):
143	
144	![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/traveller59/second.pytorch/master/images/kittibox.png)
145	
146	For each box, the dimensions are $(w, l, h)$, and the reference direction for the yaw angle is the positive direction of the y axis. For more details, refer to the [repo](https://github.com/traveller59/second.pytorch#concepts).
147	
148	Our LiDAR coordinate system has two changes:
149	
150	- The yaw angle is defined to be right-handed instead of left-handed for consistency;

152	
153	### Waymo
154	
155	We use the KITTI-format data of Waymo dataset. Therefore, KITTI and Waymo also share the same coordinate system in our implementation.
156	
157	### NuScenes
158

164	
165	Lyft shares the same data format with NuScenes as far as coordinate system is involved.

168	
169	### ScanNet
170	
171	The raw data of ScanNet is not point cloud but mesh. The sampled point cloud data is under our depth coordinate system. For ScanNet detection task, the box annotations are axis-aligned, and the yaw angle is always zero. 172

174

182

184	
185	### Box conversion (between different coordinate systems)
186	
187	Take the conversion between our Camera coordinate system and LiDAR coordinate system as an example:
188	
189	First, for points and box centers, the coordinates before and after the conversion satisfy the following relationship:
190	
191	- $x\_{LiDAR}=z\_{camera}$
192	- $y\_{LiDAR}=-x\_{camera}$
193	- $z\_{LiDAR}=-y\_{camera}$
194	
195	Then, the box dimensions before and after the conversion satisfy the following relationship:
196	
197	- $dx\_{LiDAR}=dx\_{camera}$
198	- $dy\_{LiDAR}=dz\_{camera}$
199	- $dz\_{LiDAR}=dy\_{camera}$
200	
201	Finally, the yaw angle should also be converted:
202	
203	- $r\_{LiDAR}=-\\frac{\\pi}{2}-r\_{camera}$
204	
205	See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/box_3d_mode.py) for more details.
206	
207	### Bird's Eye View
208	
209	The BEV of a camera coordinate system box is $(x, z, dx, dz, -r)$ if the 3D box is $(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)$. The inversion of the sign of the yaw angle is because the positive direction of the gravity axis of the Camera coordinate system points to the ground.
210	
211	See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/cam_box3d.py) for more details.
212	
213	### Rotation of boxes
214	
215	We set the rotation of all kinds of boxes to be counter-clockwise about the gravity axis. Therefore, to rotate a 3D box we first calculate the new box center, and then we add the rotation angle to the yaw angle.
216	
217	See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/cam_box3d.py) for more details.
218	
219	## Common FAQ
220	
221	#### Q1: Are the box related ops universal to all coordinate system types?
222	
223	No. For example, [RoI-Aware Pooling ops](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmcv/blob/master/mmcv/ops/roiaware_pool3d.py) is applicable to boxes under Depth or LiDAR coordinate system only. The evaluation functions for KITTI dataset [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/evaluation/kitti_utils) are only applicable to boxes under Camera coordinate system since the rotation is clockwise if viewed from above.
224	
225	For each box related op, we have marked the type of boxes to which we can apply the op.
226	
227	#### Q2: In every coordinate system, do the three axes point exactly to the right, the front, and the ground, respectively?
228	
229	No. For example, in KITTI, we need a calibration matrix when converting from Camera coordinate system to LiDAR coordinate system.
230	
231	#### Q3: How does a phase difference of $2\\pi$ in the yaw angle of a box affect evaluation?
232	
233	For IoU calculation, a phase difference of $2\\pi$ in the yaw angle will result in the same box, thus not affecting evaluation.
234	
235	For angle prediction evaluation such as the NDS metric in NuScenes and the AOS metric in KITTI, the angle of predicted boxes will be first standardized, so the phase difference of $2\\pi$ will not change the result.
236	
237	#### Q4: How does a phase difference of $\\pi$ in the yaw angle of a box affect evaluation?
238	
239	For IoU calculation, a phase difference of $\\pi$ in the yaw angle will result in the same box, thus not affecting evaluation.
240	
241	However, for angle prediction evaluation, this will result in the exact opposite direction.
242	
243	Just think about a car. The yaw angle is the angle between the direction of the car front and the positive direction of the x-axis. If we add $\\pi$ to this angle, the car front will become the car rear.
244	
245	For categories such as barrier, the front and the rear have no difference, therefore a phase difference of $\\pi$ will not affect the angle prediction score.
246

                      |  /
                      | /
                      |/

The definition of the yaw angle of a box is illustrated in the figure below.

y front

 /|\        ^
  |        /|\
  |     ____|____
  |    |    |    |

### KITTI

In SECOND, the LiDAR coordinate system for a box is defined as follows (a bird's eye view):

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/traveller59/second.pytorch/master/images/kittibox.png)

- The yaw angle is defined to be right-handed instead of left-handed for consistency;

### Waymo

We use the KITTI-format data of Waymo dataset. Therefore, KITTI and Waymo also share the same coordinate system in our implementation.

### NuScenes

NuScenes provides a toolkit for evaluation, in which each box is wrapped into a `Box` instance. The coordinate system of `Box` is different from our LiDAR coordinate system in that the first two elements of the box dimension correspond to $(dy, dx)$, or $(w, l)$, respectively, instead of the reverse. For more details, please refer to the NuScenes [tutorial](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/docs/en/datasets/nuscenes_det.md#notes).

### Lyft

Lyft shares the same data format with NuScenes as far as coordinate system is involved.

Please refer to the [official website](https://www.kaggle.com/c/3d-object-detection-for-autonomous-vehicles/data) for more information.

### ScanNet

The raw data of ScanNet is not point cloud but mesh. The sampled point cloud data is under our depth coordinate system. For ScanNet detection task, the box annotations are axis-aligned, and the yaw angle is always zero. Therefore the direction of the yaw angle in our depth coordinate system makes no difference regarding ScanNet.

### SUN RGB-D

The raw data of SUN RGB-D is not point cloud but RGB-D image. By back projection, we obtain the corresponding point cloud for each image, which is under our Depth coordinate system. However, the annotation is not under our system and thus needs conversion.

For the conversion from raw annotation to annotation under our Depth coordinate system, please refer to [sunrgbd_data_utils.py](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/tools/dataset_converters/sunrgbd_data_utils.py).

## Examples

### Box conversion (between different coordinate systems)

Take the conversion between our Camera coordinate system and LiDAR coordinate system as an example:

First, for points and box centers, the coordinates before and after the conversion satisfy the following relationship:

- $x\_{LiDAR}=z\_{camera}$
- $y\_{LiDAR}=-x\_{camera}$
- $z\_{LiDAR}=-y\_{camera}$

Then, the box dimensions before and after the conversion satisfy the following relationship:

- $dx\_{LiDAR}=dx\_{camera}$
- $dy\_{LiDAR}=dz\_{camera}$
- $dz\_{LiDAR}=dy\_{camera}$

Finally, the yaw angle should also be converted:

- $r\_{LiDAR}=-\\frac{\\pi}{2}-r\_{camera}$

See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/box_3d_mode.py) for more details.

### Bird's Eye View

The BEV of a camera coordinate system box is $(x, z, dx, dz, -r)$ if the 3D box is $(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)$. The inversion of the sign of the yaw angle is because the positive direction of the gravity axis of the Camera coordinate system points to the ground.

See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/cam_box3d.py) for more details.

### Rotation of boxes

We set the rotation of all kinds of boxes to be counter-clockwise about the gravity axis. Therefore, to rotate a 3D box we first calculate the new box center, and then we add the rotation angle to the yaw angle.

See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/cam_box3d.py) for more details.

## Common FAQ

#### Q1: Are the box related ops universal to all coordinate system types?

No. For example, [RoI-Aware Pooling ops](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmcv/blob/master/mmcv/ops/roiaware_pool3d.py) is applicable to boxes under Depth or LiDAR coordinate system only. The evaluation functions for KITTI dataset [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/evaluation/kitti_utils) are only applicable to boxes under Camera coordinate system since the rotation is clockwise if viewed from above.

For each box related op, we have marked the type of boxes to which we can apply the op.

#### Q2: In every coordinate system, do the three axes point exactly to the right, the front, and the ground, respectively?

No. For example, in KITTI, we need a calibration matrix when converting from Camera coordinate system to LiDAR coordinate system.

#### Q3: How does a phase difference of $2\\pi$ in the yaw angle of a box affect evaluation?

For IoU calculation, a phase difference of $2\\pi$ in the yaw angle will result in the same box, thus not affecting evaluation.

For angle prediction evaluation such as the NDS metric in NuScenes and the AOS metric in KITTI, the angle of predicted boxes will be first standardized, so the phase difference of $2\\pi$ will not change the result.

#### Q4: How does a phase difference of $\\pi$ in the yaw angle of a box affect evaluation?

For IoU calculation, a phase difference of $\\pi$ in the yaw angle will result in the same box, thus not affecting evaluation.

However, for angle prediction evaluation, this will result in the exact opposite direction.

Just think about a car. The yaw angle is the angle between the direction of the car front and the positive direction of the x-axis. If we add $\\pi$ to this angle, the car front will become the car rear.

For categories such as barrier, the front and the rear have no difference, therefore a phase difference of $\\pi$ will not affect the angle prediction score.

1	# Coordinate System
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	MMDetection3D uses three different coordinate systems. The existence of different coordinate systems in the society of 3D object detection is necessary, because for various 3D data collection devices, such as LiDAR, depth camera, etc., the coordinate systems are not consistent, and different 3D datasets also follow different data formats. Early works, such as SECOND, VoteNet, convert the raw data to another format, forming conventions that some later works also follow, making the conversion between coordinate systems even more complicated.
6	
7	Despite the variety of datasets and equipment, by summarizing the line of works on 3D object detection we can roughly categorize coordinate systems into three:
8	
9	- Camera coordinate system -- the coordinate system of most cameras, in which the positive direction of the y-axis points to the ground, the positive direction of the x-axis points to the right, and the positive direction of the z-axis points to the front.
10	
11	  ```
12	             up  z front
13	              |    ^
14	              |   /
15	              |  /
16	              | /
17	              |/
18	  left ------ 0 ------> x right
19	              |
20	              |
21	              |
22	              |
23	              v
24	            y down
25	  ```
26	
27	- LiDAR coordinate system -- the coordinate system of many LiDARs, in which the negative direction of the z-axis points to the ground, the positive direction of the x-axis points to the front, and the positive direction of the y-axis points to the left.
28	
29	  ```
30	               z up  x front
31	                 ^    ^
32	                 |   /
33	                 |  /
34	                 | /
35	                 |/
36	  y left <------ 0 ------ right
37	  ```
38	
39	- Depth coordinate system -- the coordinate system used by VoteNet, H3DNet, etc., in which the negative direction of the z-axis points to the ground, the positive direction of the x-axis points to the right, and the positive direction of the y-axis points to the front.
40	
41	  ```
42	            z up  y front
43	              ^    ^
44	              |   /
45	              |  /
46	              | /
47	              |/
48	  left ------ 0 ------> x right
49	  ```
50	
51	The definition of coordinate systems in this tutorial is actually **more than just defining the three axes**. For a box in the form of $(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)$, our coordinate systems also define how to interpret the box dimensions $(dx, dy, dz)$ and the yaw angle $r$.
52	
53	The illustration of the three coordinate systems is shown below:
54	
55	![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/master/resources/coord_sys_all.png)
56	
57	The three figures above are the 3D coordinate systems while the three figures below are the bird's eye view.
58	
59	We will stick to the three coordinate systems defined in this tutorial in the future.
60	
61	## Definition of the yaw angle
62	
63	Please refer to [wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_angles#Tait%E2%80%93Bryan_angles) for the standard definition of the yaw angle. In object detection, we choose an axis as the gravity axis, and a reference direction on the plane $\\Pi$ perpendicular to the gravity axis, then the reference direction has a yaw angle of 0, and other directions on $\\Pi$ have non-zero yaw angles depending on its angle with the reference direction.
64	
65	Currently, for all supported datasets, annotations do not include pitch angle and roll angle, which means we need only consider the yaw angle when predicting boxes and calculating overlap between boxes.
66	
67	In MMDetection3D, all three coordinate systems are right-handed coordinate systems, which means the ascending direction of the yaw angle is counter-clockwise if viewed from the negative direction of the gravity axis (the axis is pointing at one's eyes).
68	
69	The figure below shows that, in this right-handed coordinate system, if we set the positive direction of the x-axis as a reference direction, then the positive direction of the y-axis has a yaw angle of $\\frac{\\pi}{2}$.
70	
71	```
72	                     z up  y front (yaw=0.5*pi)
73	                      ^    ^
74	                      |   /
75	                      |  /
76	                      | /
77	                      |/
78	left (yaw=pi)  ------ 0 ------> x right (yaw=0)
79	```
80	
81	For a box, the value of its yaw angle equals its direction minus a reference direction. In all three coordinate systems in MMDetection3D, the reference direction is always the positive direction of the x-axis, while the direction of a box is defined to be parallel with the x-axis if its yaw angle is 0. The definition of the yaw angle of a box is illustrated in the figure below.
82	
83	```
84	y front
85	  ^      box direction (yaw=0.5*pi)
86	 /|\        ^
87	  |        /|\
88	  |     ____|____
89	  |    |    |    |
90	  |    |    |    |
91	__|____|____|____|______\ x right
92	  |    |    |    |      /
93	  |    |    |    |
94	  |    |____|____|
95	  |
96	```
97	
98	## Definition of the box dimensions
99	
100	The definition of the box dimensions cannot be disentangled with the definition of the yaw angle. In the previous section, we said that the direction of a box is defined to be parallel with the x-axis if its yaw angle is 0. Then naturally, the dimension of a box which corresponds to the x-axis should be $dx$. However, this is not always the case in some datasets (we will address that later).
101	
102	The following figures show the meaning of the correspondence between the x-axis and $dx$, and between the y-axis and $dy$.
103	
104	```
105	y front
106	  ^      box direction (yaw=0.5*pi)
107	 /|\        ^
108	  |        /|\
109	  |     ____|____
110	  |    |    |    |
111	  |    |    |    | dx
112	__|____|____|____|______\ x right
113	  |    |    |    |      /
114	  |    |    |    |
115	  |    |____|____|
116	  |         dy
117	```
118	
119	Note that the box direction is always parallel with the edge $dx$.
120	
121	```
122	y front
123	  ^     _________
124	 /|\   |    |    |
125	  |    |    |    |
126	  |    |    |    | dy
127	  |    |____|____|____\  box direction (yaw=0)
128	  |    |    |    |    /
129	__|____|____|____|_________\ x right
130	  |    |    |    |         /
131	  |    |____|____|
132	  |         dx
133	  |
134	```
135	
136	## Relation with raw coordinate systems of supported datasets
137	
138	### KITTI
139	
140	The raw annotation of KITTI is under camera coordinate system, see [get_label_anno](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/tools/dataset_converters/kitti_data_utils.py). In MMDetection3D, to train LiDAR-based models on KITTI, the data is first converted from camera coordinate system to LiDAR coordinate system, see [get_ann_info](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/datasets/kitti_dataset.py). For training vision-based models, the data is kept in the camera coordinate system.
141	
142	In SECOND, the LiDAR coordinate system for a box is defined as follows (a bird's eye view):
143	
144	![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/traveller59/second.pytorch/master/images/kittibox.png)
145	
146	For each box, the dimensions are $(w, l, h)$, and the reference direction for the yaw angle is the positive direction of the y axis. For more details, refer to the [repo](https://github.com/traveller59/second.pytorch#concepts).
147	
148	Our LiDAR coordinate system has two changes:
149	
150	- The yaw angle is defined to be right-handed instead of left-handed for consistency;
151	- The box dimensions are $(l, w, h)$ instead of $(w, l, h)$, since $w$ corresponds to $dy$ and $l$ corresponds to $dx$ in KITTI.
152	
153	### Waymo
154	
155	We use the KITTI-format data of Waymo dataset. Therefore, KITTI and Waymo also share the same coordinate system in our implementation.
156	
157	### NuScenes
158	
159	NuScenes provides a toolkit for evaluation, in which each box is wrapped into a `Box` instance. The coordinate system of `Box` is different from our LiDAR coordinate system in that the first two elements of the box dimension correspond to $(dy, dx)$, or $(w, l)$, respectively, instead of the reverse. For more details, please refer to the NuScenes [tutorial](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/docs/en/datasets/nuscenes_det.md#notes).
160	
161	Readers may refer to the [NuScenes development kit](https://github.com/nutonomy/nuscenes-devkit/tree/master/python-sdk/nuscenes/eval/detection) for the definition of a [NuScenes box](https://github.com/nutonomy/nuscenes-devkit/blob/2c6a752319f23910d5f55cc995abc547a9e54142/python-sdk/nuscenes/utils/data_classes.py#L457) and implementation of [NuScenes evaluation](https://github.com/nutonomy/nuscenes-devkit/blob/master/python-sdk/nuscenes/eval/detection/evaluate.py).
162	
163	### Lyft
164	
165	Lyft shares the same data format with NuScenes as far as coordinate system is involved.
166	
167	Please refer to the [official website](https://www.kaggle.com/c/3d-object-detection-for-autonomous-vehicles/data) for more information.
168	
169	### ScanNet
170	
171	The raw data of ScanNet is not point cloud but mesh. The sampled point cloud data is under our depth coordinate system. For ScanNet detection task, the box annotations are axis-aligned, and the yaw angle is always zero. Therefore the direction of the yaw angle in our depth coordinate system makes no difference regarding ScanNet.
172	
173	### SUN RGB-D
174	
175	The raw data of SUN RGB-D is not point cloud but RGB-D image. By back projection, we obtain the corresponding point cloud for each image, which is under our Depth coordinate system. However, the annotation is not under our system and thus needs conversion.
176	
177	For the conversion from raw annotation to annotation under our Depth coordinate system, please refer to [sunrgbd_data_utils.py](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/tools/dataset_converters/sunrgbd_data_utils.py).
178	
179	### S3DIS
180	
181	S3DIS shares the same coordinate system as ScanNet in our implementation. However, S3DIS is a segmentation-task-only dataset, and thus no annotation is coordinate system sensitive.
182	
183	## Examples
184	
185	### Box conversion (between different coordinate systems)
186	
187	Take the conversion between our Camera coordinate system and LiDAR coordinate system as an example:
188	
189	First, for points and box centers, the coordinates before and after the conversion satisfy the following relationship:
190	
191	- $x\_{LiDAR}=z\_{camera}$
192	- $y\_{LiDAR}=-x\_{camera}$
193	- $z\_{LiDAR}=-y\_{camera}$
194	
195	Then, the box dimensions before and after the conversion satisfy the following relationship:
196	
197	- $dx\_{LiDAR}=dx\_{camera}$
198	- $dy\_{LiDAR}=dz\_{camera}$
199	- $dz\_{LiDAR}=dy\_{camera}$
200	
201	Finally, the yaw angle should also be converted:
202	
203	- $r\_{LiDAR}=-\\frac{\\pi}{2}-r\_{camera}$
204	
205	See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/box_3d_mode.py) for more details.
206	
207	### Bird's Eye View
208	
209	The BEV of a camera coordinate system box is $(x, z, dx, dz, -r)$ if the 3D box is $(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)$. The inversion of the sign of the yaw angle is because the positive direction of the gravity axis of the Camera coordinate system points to the ground.
210	
211	See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/cam_box3d.py) for more details.
212	
213	### Rotation of boxes
214	
215	We set the rotation of all kinds of boxes to be counter-clockwise about the gravity axis. Therefore, to rotate a 3D box we first calculate the new box center, and then we add the rotation angle to the yaw angle.
216	
217	See the code [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/bbox/structures/cam_box3d.py) for more details.
218	
219	## Common FAQ
220	
221	#### Q1: Are the box related ops universal to all coordinate system types?
222	
223	No. For example, [RoI-Aware Pooling ops](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmcv/blob/master/mmcv/ops/roiaware_pool3d.py) is applicable to boxes under Depth or LiDAR coordinate system only. The evaluation functions for KITTI dataset [here](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/master/mmdet3d/core/evaluation/kitti_utils) are only applicable to boxes under Camera coordinate system since the rotation is clockwise if viewed from above.
224	
225	For each box related op, we have marked the type of boxes to which we can apply the op.
226	
227	#### Q2: In every coordinate system, do the three axes point exactly to the right, the front, and the ground, respectively?
228	
229	No. For example, in KITTI, we need a calibration matrix when converting from Camera coordinate system to LiDAR coordinate system.
230	
231	#### Q3: How does a phase difference of $2\\pi$ in the yaw angle of a box affect evaluation?
232	
233	For IoU calculation, a phase difference of $2\\pi$ in the yaw angle will result in the same box, thus not affecting evaluation.
234	
235	For angle prediction evaluation such as the NDS metric in NuScenes and the AOS metric in KITTI, the angle of predicted boxes will be first standardized, so the phase difference of $2\\pi$ will not change the result.
236	
237	#### Q4: How does a phase difference of $\\pi$ in the yaw angle of a box affect evaluation?
238	
239	For IoU calculation, a phase difference of $\\pi$ in the yaw angle will result in the same box, thus not affecting evaluation.
240	
241	However, for angle prediction evaluation, this will result in the exact opposite direction.
242	
243	Just think about a car. The yaw angle is the angle between the direction of the car front and the positive direction of the x-axis. If we add $\\pi$ to this angle, the car front will become the car rear.
244	
245	For categories such as barrier, the front and the rear have no difference, therefore a phase difference of $\\pi$ will not affect the angle prediction score.

# Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
from typing import Optional, Sequence, Union

import numpy as np
from torch import Tensor

from .base_points import BasePoints


class LiDARPoints(BasePoints):
    """Points of instances in LIDAR coordinates.

    Args:
        tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[Sequence[float]]): The points
            data with shape (N, points_dim).
        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
            is (x, y, z, ...). Defaults to 3.
        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
            extra dimension. Defaults to None.

    Attributes:
        tensor (Tensor): Float matrix with shape (N, points_dim).
        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
            is (x, y, z, ...).
        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
            extra dimension. Defaults to None.
        rotation_axis (int): Default rotation axis for points rotation.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray, Sequence[Sequence[float]]],
                 points_dim: int = 3,
                 attribute_dims: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        super(LiDARPoints, self).__init__(
            tensor, points_dim=points_dim, attribute_dims=attribute_dims)
        self.rotation_axis = 2

    def flip(self, bev_direction: str = 'horizontal') -> None:
        """Flip the points along given BEV direction.

        Args:
            bev_direction (str): Flip direction (horizontal or vertical).
                Defaults to 'horizontal'.
        """
        assert bev_direction in ('horizontal', 'vertical')
        if bev_direction == 'horizontal':
            self.tensor[:, 1] = -self.tensor[:, 1]

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import Tensor

from mmdet3d.utils import array_converter


@array_converter(apply_to=('val', ))
def limit_period(val: Union[np.ndarray, Tensor],
                 offset: float = 0.5,
                 period: float = np.pi) -> Union[np.ndarray, Tensor]:
    """Limit the value into a period for periodic function.

    Args:
        val (np.ndarray or Tensor): The value to be converted.
        offset (float): Offset to set the value range. Defaults to 0.5.
        period (float): Period of the value. Defaults to np.pi.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray or Tensor: Value in the range of
        [-offset * period, (1-offset) * period].
    """
    limited_val = val - torch.floor(val / period + offset) * period
    return limited_val


@array_converter(apply_to=('points', 'angles'))
def rotation_3d_in_axis(
    points: Union[np.ndarray, Tensor],
    angles: Union[np.ndarray, Tensor, float],
    axis: int = 0,
    return_mat: bool = False,
    clockwise: bool = False
) -> Union[Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray], Tuple[Tensor, Tensor], np.ndarray,
           Tensor]:
    """Rotate points by angles according to axis.

    Args:
        points (np.ndarray or Tensor): Points with shape (N, M, 3).
        angles (np.ndarray or Tensor or float): Vector of angles with shape
            (N, ).
        axis (int): The axis to be rotated. Defaults to 0.
        return_mat (bool): Whether or not to return the rotation matrix
            (transposed). Defaults to False.
        clockwise (bool): Whether the rotation is clockwise. Defaults to False.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the axis is not in range [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2], it
            will raise ValueError.

    Returns:
        Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] or Tuple[Tensor, Tensor] or np.ndarray or
        Tensor: Rotated points with shape (N, M, 3) and rotation matrix with
        shape (N, 3, 3).
    """
    batch_free = len(points.shape) == 2

本讲是单元 2（核心数据结构）的第一讲。在 [u1-l4](u1-l4-repository-structure-map.md) 中我们看到 `mmdet3d/structures` 位于星形依赖的最底层——本讲就从这个最底层中最重要的「坐标系约定」讲起。后面所有的数据集类（单元 3）、检测器（单元 4-6）、评估指标（单元 7）都建立在这套约定之上。

## 2. 前置知识

**为什么 3D 检测需要不止一套坐标系？**

在 2D 图像检测中，坐标约定几乎只有一种：原点在左上角，x 向右，y 向下。但 3D 世界里的数据来自不同物理设备，每台设备自带一套「出厂坐标」：

- **LiDAR（激光雷达）** 通常以自身旋转轴为 z 轴（朝上），前进方向为 x 轴。
- **相机** 遵循计算机视觉惯例：光轴为 z 轴（朝前），图像右方向为 x 轴，下方向为 y 轴。
- **深度相机 / RGB-D 数据**（如室内场景的 Kinect）产生的点云常用另一种约定：z 朝上，y 朝前。

此外，不同数据集与经典论文也各自「站队」：SECOND 等室外 LiDAR 方法用 LiDAR 系，VoteNet 等室内方法用 Depth 系，KITTI 原始标注却是相机系。MMDetection3D 不强行统一成一套，而是把三种约定都显式建模出来，并提供两者之间互转的工具——这就是本讲的两个主角 `Box3DMode` 与 `Coord3DMode`。

**回顾：7 自由度 3D 框。** 在 [u1-l3](u1-l3-first-inference-demo.md) 中我们已经见过，一个 3D 框由 7 个数描述：

\[
(x,\ y,\ z,\ dx,\ dy,\ dz,\ r)
\]

- \((x, y, z)\)：框的底部中心（bottom center）坐标；
- \((dx, dy, dz)\)：框沿三个坐标轴方向的边长（尺寸）；
- \(r\)：yaw 角（偏航角），即框在水平面内的朝向。

注意：这 7 个数的「含义」依赖坐标系——同样是 \(dx\)，在 LiDAR 系里是沿「前方」的边长，在相机系里是沿「右方」的边长。所以坐标系转换必须同时处理坐标、尺寸、yaw 三个量，缺一不可。

**yaw 的统一定义。** MMDetection3D 中三个坐标系都是右手系。取重力轴（LiDAR/DEPTH 的 z 轴、CAM 的 y 轴），在其垂直平面 \(\Pi\) 上取 x 轴正方向为参考方向（yaw = 0），yaw 角随方向逆时针（从重力轴负方向望向原点时）递增。一个框 yaw = 0 意味着它的「朝向边 \(dx\)」与 x 轴平行。官方文档用一句口诀概括：**框的朝向永远与 \(dx\) 边平行**。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 三大坐标系的方向约定

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

三个坐标系的方向图直接写在 `Box3DMode` 的类文档字符串里，这是全库最权威的定义处：

- **LIDAR**：z 朝上，x 朝前，y 朝左。用于 KITTI/nuScenes/Waymo 等 LiDAR 数据与 SECOND、PointPillars、CenterPoint 等室外算法。
- **CAM**：x 朝右，y 朝下，z 朝前。用于单目 3D 检测（FCOS3D、SMOKE）与 KITTI 原始标注。
- **DEPTH**：z 朝上，y 朝前，x 朝右。用于 ScanNet、SUN RGB-D 等室内数据与 VoteNet、H3DNet 等室内算法。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把三个坐标系的关键差异整理成一张对照表：

| | LIDAR | CAM | DEPTH |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 上 | z | —（y 朝下） | z |
| 前 | x | z | y |
| 右/左 | y 朝左 | x 朝右 | x 朝右 |
| 重力轴（yaw 旋转轴） | z（axis=2） | y（axis=1） | z（axis=2） |
| 框底部中心的相对坐标 | (0.5, 0.5, 0) | (0.5, 1.0, 0.5) | (0.5, 0.5, 0) |
| 典型场景 | 室外 LiDAR 检测 | 单目 3D / KITTI 原始标注 | 室内点云检测 |

「底部中心的相对坐标」指框内一点在框自身归一化坐标系里的位置：LiDAR/DEPTH 框的 \((x,y,z)\) 指底部面中心（z 在框的最低面），而 CAM 框因 y 朝下，\((x,y,z)\) 指的是几何中心。这解释了为什么 CAM 的相对坐标是 (0.5, 1.0, 0.5)——沿 y 方向覆盖整个高度。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：在 LiDAR 坐标系中，一辆车头指向 -y 轴（正左方）的车，yaw 是多少？

**答案**：\(+\frac{\pi}{2}\)。LiDAR 系 z 朝上，从上方（z 轴负方向）俯视，x 前 y 左是逆时针方向，yaw 逆时针为正；从 x 正方向逆时针转 90° 正好指向 y 正方向（左）。源码文档 [box_3d_mode.py:L24](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L24) 的图里明确标注了 `(yaw=0.5*pi) left y`。

**练习 2**：为什么 CAM 坐标系的 yaw 旋转轴是 axis=1（y 轴），而 LIDAR 是 axis=2（z 轴）？

**答案**：yaw 定义为绕「重力轴」的旋转。LiDAR 与 DEPTH 系中 z 轴朝上（重力轴），是第 3 个分量（索引 2）；CAM 系中 y 轴朝下指向地面，重力轴是第 2 个分量（索引 1）。见 [box_3d_mode.py:L30-L31](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L30-L31) 与 [L46-L47](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L46-L47)。

### 4.2 Box3DMode：框坐标系转换的引擎

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`Box3DMode.convert` 是一个静态方法，负责把任意 `src` 模式的 3D 框转换到 `dst` 模式。它解决的核心问题是：**同一个物理框，在不同坐标系下，7 个参数要同时重写**。它接受四种输入（tuple/list、numpy 数组、Tensor、`BaseInstance3DBoxes` 实例），返回同类型的结果——如果你传入的是 `LiDARInstance3DBoxes`，它会返回 `CameraInstance3DBoxes` 等目标坐标系对应的子类。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

转换分三步（以 LIDAR → CAM 为例）：

```text
输入 (x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)  @ LiDAR
  │
  ├─ ① 中心坐标：乘旋转矩阵 rt_mat（默认 [[0,-1,0],[0,0,-1],[1,0,0]]）
  │      x_cam = -y_lidar,  y_cam = -z_lidar,  z_cam = x_lidar
  │      等价写法：x_L = z_C, y_L = -x_C, z_L = -y_C
  │
  ├─ ② 尺寸重排：(dx, dy, dz) → (dx, dz, dy)     # y、z 互换
  │      因为 LiDAR 的 dz（高度）对应 CAM 的 dy（深度方向边长）
  │
  └─ ③ yaw 变换：r_cam = -r_lidar - π/2，再 limit_period 到 [-π, π)
  │
输出 (x', y', z', dx', dy', dz', r')  @ CAM
```

六个转换方向中 yaw 的变换公式汇总：

| 方向 | yaw 公式 | 尺寸重排 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LIDAR → CAM | \(r' = -r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| CAM → LIDAR | \(r' = -r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| DEPTH → CAM | \(r' = -r\)（纯符号翻转） | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| CAM → DEPTH | \(r' = -r\)（纯符号翻转） | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| LIDAR → DEPTH | \(r' = r + \frac{\pi}{2}\) | 不变 \((dx, dy, dz)\) |
| DEPTH → LIDAR | \(r' = r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) | 不变 \((dx, dy, dz)\) |

`limit_period` 的数学定义：把值限制在 \([-offset \times period,\ (1-offset) \times period)\) 内，转换中用 `period=2π`，即把 yaw 归一化到 \([-π, π)\)。计算方式为：

\[
limited\_val = val - \lfloor val / period + offset \rfloor \times period
\]

之所以出现 \(-r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) 这样的公式，是因为两个坐标系的参考方向与旋转正方向都不同：先取负号修正「逆时针/顺时针」的差异，再平移 \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) 修正「x 前方 vs x 右方」的参考方向差异。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：一个 LiDAR 系中的框 yaw = 0.6，转换到 CAM 系后 yaw 是多少？再转回 LiDAR 系呢？

**答案**：CAM 系 yaw \(= -0.6 - \frac{\pi}{2} \approx -2.1708\)（在 \([-π, π)\) 内，`limit_period` 不再调整）。转回 LiDAR 时套 CAM→LIDAR 公式：\(-(-2.1708) - \frac{\pi}{2} = 2.1708 - 1.5708 = 0.6\)，往返还原——转换是可逆的。

**练习 2**：为什么 LIDAR → DEPTH 不需要交换尺寸，而 LIDAR → CAM 需要？

**答案**：LIDAR 与 DEPTH 的重力轴都是 z，水平面内两个方向都是「前/右」互换（x↔y），所以 \((dx, dy)\) 各自对应另一系里的「前向边/右向边」，语义连贯，无需交换（对比 [box_3d_mode.py:L188](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L188) 的 `torch.cat([x_size, y_size, z_size])`）；而 CAM 的重力轴是 y，LiDAR 的高度 dz 在 CAM 里变成沿 y 的边长，所以必须交换 y、z 两个尺寸分量（[L130](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L130)）。

**练习 3**：`rt_mat` 传 `None` 与传一个 3×4 的真实标定矩阵，`convert` 的行为有何不同？

**答案**：`rt_mat=None` 时使用「理想轴向对齐」的默认旋转矩阵，只做轴重排，不含平移（L128-L129 等六处）；传入 3×4 矩阵时走 [L222-L225](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L222-L225) 的齐次坐标路径，坐标还会被平移（传感器不在同一点时必需），且此时通常应同时设 `correct_yaw=True` 走向量旋转路径重算 yaw。

### 4.3 Coord3DMode：框与点的统一转换入口

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`Box3DMode` 只能转框；但 3D 场景里点云也要跟着一起换坐标系（比如把 LiDAR 点云投影到相机画 Fig）。`Coord3DMode` 在 `Box3DMode` 之上做了一层「类型分发」：看到 `BaseInstance3DBoxes` 就转框，看到 `BasePoints` 就转点，看到裸数组按 `is_point` 标志决定。**转框的逻辑它并不重写，而是原样委托给 `Box3DMode.convert`**——所以两个枚举的六个方向矩阵完全一致。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
Coord3DMode.convert(input, src, dst, ...)
  │
  ├─ input 是 BaseInstance3DBoxes ──► convert_box ──► Box3DMode.convert（4.2 已讲）
  ├─ input 是 BasePoints ──────────► convert_point（点云专用）
  └─ input 是裸 tensor/ndarray/list
        ├─ is_point=True（默认）──► convert_point
        └─ is_point=False ────────► convert_box
```

`convert_point` 比转框简单得多：点没有尺寸和 yaw，只需把每个点的前 3 维坐标乘 `rt_mat`，**其余维度（强度、颜色、时间戳等属性列）原样保留**。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

[coord_3d_mode.py:L104-L127](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L104-L127) —— `convert` 的类型分发逻辑：L104-L111 处理框、L112-L113 处理点对象、L114-L125 处理裸数组（依 `is_point` 分流）、L126-L127 其余类型直接抛 `NotImplementedError`。

[coord_3d_mode.py:L129-L168](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L129-L168) —— `convert_box` 只是薄薄一层包装，函数体直接 `return Box3DMode.convert(...)`（L162-L168），验证了「不重复实现」的设计。

[coord_3d_mode.py:L216-L233](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L216-L233) —— `convert_point` 中六个方向的默认旋转矩阵，与 `Box3DMode.convert` 中的矩阵逐个相同（对照 [box_3d_mode.py:L127-L214](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L127-L214)）。例如 LIDAR→CAM 同为 `[[0,-1,0],[0,0,-1],[1,0,0]]`。

[coord_3d_mode.py:L239-L249](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L239-L249) —— 点坐标变换核心：同样支持 4 列齐次矩阵（L241-L244）；L248-L249 把变换后的 \((x,y,z)\) 与原样保留的属性列 `arr[..., 3:]` 重新拼起来。**这就是多帧点云带强度、RGB 时属性不丢的原因。**

[coord_3d_mode.py:L251-L271](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L251-L271) —— 按目标模式返回 `CameraPoints` / `LiDARPoints` / `DepthPoints`，并把 `attribute_dims` 原样传给新对象（L268-L271），保证「第几列是强度/颜色」的元信息在转换后仍然有效。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

同样见 [5. 综合实践](#5-综合实践)脚本第三步：用 `Coord3DMode.convert` 分别转换框（`is_point=False`）和点（默认 `is_point=True`），对比与 `Box3DMode.convert` 的结果是否一致。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：给 `Coord3DMode.convert` 传一个形状 (N, 7) 的裸 Tensor，不设 `is_point`，会发生什么？

**答案**：默认 `is_point=True`（[coord_3d_mode.py:L74](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L74)），它会走 `convert_point`：只把前 3 列当坐标旋转，后 4 列（尺寸、yaw）被当成「属性」原样保留——得到的是错误的框。**用裸数组转框必须显式 `is_point=False`**；更稳妥的做法是直接传 `BaseInstance3DBoxes` 实例，让类型分发自动生效。

**练习 2**：`LiDARPoints` 对象的 `convert_to` 方法（[lidar_points.py:L51-L72](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/lidar_points.py#L51-L72)）与 `Coord3DMode.convert_point` 是什么关系？

**答案**：`convert_to` 是实例方法语法糖，内部就是调用 `Coord3DMode.convert_point(point=self, src=Coord3DMode.LIDAR, dst=dst, rt_mat=rt_mat)`（L70-L72）。每个 Points 子类都有对应实现，源码里各数据集、可视化模块调 `points.convert_to(...)` 时走的正是这条链。

### 4.4 BasePoints 家族与 lidar2cam 矩阵的存放

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`mmdet3d/structures/points/` 目录定义了点云的数据容器：`BasePoints` 基类加 `LiDARPoints` / `CameraPoints` / `DepthPoints` 三个坐标系子类——与框的三个子类完全平行。它回答两个问题：点云张量怎么存（`(N, points_dim)`，每行 `(x, y, z, ...)`），以及绕哪根轴旋转（`rotation_axis`）。

而「真实世界」的坐标系转换需要标定矩阵。以 KITTI 为例，`lidar2cam` 就是把 LiDAR 系坐标变到相机系 的 4×4 矩阵，它由两步复合而成：

\[
lidar2cam = R0\_rect \cdot Tr\_velo\_to\_cam
\]

其中 \(Tr\_velo\_to\_cam\) 是 Velodyne 到相机的平移旋转，\(R0\_rect\) 是相机内参修正旋转。这类矩阵在数据预处理阶段就被写进 info pkl，运行时由数据集类读取。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

一个 GT 框从原始标注到模型可用格式的路径（以 KITTI LiDAR 训练为例）：

```text
KITTI 原始标注（CAM 系）
  │  tools/create_data.py 阶段：
  │    update_infos_to_v2.py 计算 lidar2cam = R0_rect @ Tr_velo_to_cam
  │    存入 info pkl: info['images']['CAM2']['lidar2cam']
  ▼
数据集加载阶段（mmdet3d/datasets/kitti_dataset.py）
  │  取出 lidar2cam，求逆 inv(lidar2cam)（即 cam2lidar）
  │  CameraInstance3DBoxes(gt).convert_to(LIDAR, rt_mat=inv(lidar2cam))
  ▼
LiDAR 系的 DepthInstance→LiDARInstance3DBoxes，喂给 PointPillars 等模型
```

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

[base_points.py:L33-L54](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L33-L54) —— `BasePoints.__init__`：断言张量必须是二维且最后一维等于 `points_dim`（L46-L49），存 `tensor`、`points_dim`、`attribute_dims`，默认 `rotation_axis = 0`。`points_dim` 可以大于 3，多出的列由 `attribute_dims` 字典声明含义（如 `{'height': 3}`）。

[lidar_points.py:L30-L36](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/lidar_points.py#L30-L36) —— `LiDARPoints` 构造：调用父类后设 `self.rotation_axis = 2`（z 轴）。对比 `BasePoints` 的默认 0——每个坐标系子类的差异点之一就是这个旋转轴（CAM 子类为 1）。

[kitti_dataset.py:L166-L172](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/datasets/kitti_dataset.py#L166-L172) —— `lidar2cam` 的消费现场：L166 注释写明 `in kitti, lidar2cam = R0_rect @ Tr_velo_to_cam`；L167 从 `info['images']['CAM2']['lidar2cam']` 取出矩阵；L169-L171 把相机系 GT 框用**矩阵的逆**（cam→lidar）转换到 LiDAR 系。这正是 4.2 讲的 `rt_mat` 参数的真实用法——此时 `rt_mat` 含平移，走齐次坐标路径。

[update_infos_to_v2.py:L436-L437](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/tools/dataset_converters/update_infos_to_v2.py#L436-L437) —— `lidar2cam` 的生产现场（数据转换阶段）：`lidar2cam = rect @ Trv2c` 后存入 `temp_data_info['images']['CAM2']['lidar2cam']`。nuScenes 的对应逻辑在 L834、L917-L918（按相机键存入 `lidar2sensor`/`lidar2cam`）。Waymo 见 [waymo_converter.py:L462](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/tools/dataset_converters/waymo_converter.py#L462)。

[coord_3d_mode.py:L9-L10](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py#L9-L10) —— `coord_3d_mode.py` 顶部 import 四个 Points 类，体现「框模块」与「点模块」的协作：`Coord3DMode` 是二者共同的转换中枢。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

在综合实践脚本的第四步，我们把点云也一起转坐标系，并验证框中心与点使用同一矩阵得到一致结果。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`LiDARPoints` 的 `rotation_axis` 为什么是 2，`CameraPoints` 应该是多少？

**答案**：`rotation_axis` 指定刚体旋转（数据增强中的 `rotate`）绕哪根轴。LiDAR 系 z 朝上，重力轴索引为 2（[lidar_points.py:L36](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/lidar_points.py#L36)）；CameraPoints 在 `cam_points.py` 中设为 1（y 朝下为重力轴）。与 4.1 表格中「yaw 旋转轴」一致。

**练习 2**：为什么 `kitti_dataset.py` 里转 LiDAR 用的是 `np.linalg.inv(lidar2cam)` 而不是 `lidar2cam` 本身？

**答案**：矩阵名字表示的是变换方向：`lidar2cam` 把 LiDAR 坐标变到相机坐标。KITTI 原始标注本来就在相机系，要把它变到 LiDAR 系需要反方向的矩阵，即 `cam2lidar = inv(lidar2cam)`（[kitti_dataset.py:L169-L171](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/datasets/kitti_dataset.py#L169-L171)）。这是读 3D 代码的高频陷阱：看到 `xxx2yyy` 先默念「从 xxx 到 yyy」。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务**：构造一个 `LiDARInstance3DBoxes`，分别用 `Box3DMode.convert` 与 `Coord3DMode.convert` 把它转换到相机坐标系和深度坐标系，打印每次转换后的 tensor，验证 yaw 的符号翻转，并把一个点同步转换以核对一致性。

前置条件：按 [u1-l2](u1-l2-installation-and-verification.md) 完成安装，`import mmdet3d` 不报错。

**操作步骤**：把下面的脚本保存为 `coord_convert_demo.py`（示例代码，非仓库自带文件），运行 `python coord_convert_demo.py`：

```python
import math
import torch
from mmdet3d.structures.bbox_3d import (Box3DMode, Coord3DMode,
                                        LiDARInstance3DBoxes)

# 模拟一辆车：LiDAR 系下底部中心 (5, 2, -1)，尺寸 (dx=4, dy=2, dz=1.5)，yaw=0.6
box_tensor = torch.tensor([[5.0, 2.0, -1.0, 4.0, 2.0, 1.5, 0.6]])
lidar_box = LiDARInstance3DBoxes(box_tensor, box_dim=7)
print('LIDAR  :', lidar_box.tensor.numpy().round(4))

# 第 1 步：Box3DMode 转 CAM / DEPTH
cam_box = Box3DMode.convert(lidar_box, Box3DMode.LIDAR, Box3DMode.CAM)
depth_box = Box3DMode.convert(lidar_box, Box3DMode.LIDAR, Box3DMode.DEPTH)
print('CAM    :', cam_box.tensor.numpy().round(4), type(cam_box).__name__)
print('DEPTH  :', depth_box.tensor.numpy().round(4), type(depth_box).__name__)

# 第 2 步：手工验证 yaw 公式
print('yaw CAM   expect:', round(-0.6 - math.pi / 2, 4))
print('yaw DEPTH expect:', round(0.6 + math.pi / 2, 4))

# 第 3 步：Coord3DMode 做同样的框转换（应与第 1 步完全一致）
cam_box2 = Coord3DMode.convert(lidar_box, Coord3DMode.LIDAR,
                               Coord3DMode.CAM, is_point=False)
print('CAM(2) :', cam_box2.tensor.numpy().round(4))

# 第 4 步：Coord3DMode 转点，并与框中心对照
point = torch.tensor([[5.0, 2.0, -1.0]])  # 与框底部中心同位置的一个点
cam_point = Coord3DMode.convert(point, Coord3DMode.LIDAR, Coord3DMode.CAM)
print('point in CAM:', cam_point.numpy().round(4))
```

**需要观察的现象与预期结果**（可先笔算再对照输出）：

1. **中心坐标**：LIDAR→CAM 后应为 \((-2, 1, 5)\)，即 \(x_{cam}=-y_{lidar},\ y_{cam}=-z_{lidar},\ z_{cam}=x_{lidar}\)。
2. **尺寸**：CAM 下应为 \((4, 1.5, 2)\)——y、z 两个尺寸分量互换，dy 从 2 变成 1.5；DEPTH 下尺寸不变，仍为 \((4, 2, 1.5)\)。
3. **yaw 翻转**：CAM 下 \(r' = -0.6 - \frac{\pi}{2} \approx -2.1708\)；DEPTH 下 \(r' = 0.6 + \frac{\pi}{2} \approx +2.1708\)。两值恰好互为相反数——因为两条路径的差别正是 DEPTH→CAM 的纯翻转 \(r' = -r\)。
4. **返回类型**：`cam_box` 是 `CameraInstance3DBoxes`，`depth_box` 是 `DepthInstance3DBoxes`（[box_3d_mode.py:L254-L260](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L254-L260) 的装箱逻辑）。
5. **第 3 步与第 1 步输出逐位相同**：证明 `Coord3DMode.convert_box` 只是委托 `Box3DMode.convert`。
6. **第 4 步**：点 \((5, 2, -1)\) 转到 CAM 为 \((-2, 1, 5)\)，与框中心完全一致——同一物理位置，框和点走各自的转换函数，结果必须吻合。

若输出与上述数值不符，先检查 `box_dim` 是否为 7、是否误用了 `is_point` 默认值。本实践在纯 CPU 上即可运行，无需 GPU 与数据集。（具体打印格式因 PyTorch 版本略有差异，数值以四舍五入到 4 位小数为准；待本地验证。）

## 6. 本讲小结

- MMDetection3D 显式建模三套右手坐标系：**LIDAR**（x 前 y 左 z 上，室外 LiDAR）、**CAM**（x 右 y 下 z 前，单目/KITTI 原始标注）、**DEPTH**（x 右 y 前 z 上，室内点云）；三者的重力轴与 yaw 旋转轴分别为 z/y/z。
- 一个 3D 框的 7 参数 \((x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)\) 的**语义依赖坐标系**，转换必须同时改写坐标（乘 `rt_mat`）、尺寸（重排分量）与 yaw（公式变换 + `limit_period` 归一到 \([-π, π)\)）。
- `Box3DMode.convert` 是框转换引擎，输入输出类型保持一致（传子类实例则返回目标坐标系子类）；`rt_mat` 支持 3×3 与含平移的 3×4/4×4，任意旋转时应配 `correct_yaw=True`。
- `Coord3DMode.convert` 是统一入口：按输入类型自动分发，框转换委托 `Box3DMode`，点转换只旋转前 3 维并原样保留属性列；裸数组转框必须显式 `is_point=False`。
- 点云容器 `BasePoints` 家族与框的三个子类平行，`rotation_axis`（2/1/2）记录各自的旋转轴；`LiDARPoints.convert_to` 是 `Coord3DMode.convert_point` 的语法糖。
- 真实跨传感器转换依赖标定矩阵：KITTI 中 `lidar2cam = R0_rect @ Tr_velo_to_cam`，由 `tools/dataset_converters/update_infos_to_v2.py` 写入 info pkl 的 `info['images']['CAM2']['lidar2cam']`，运行时由 `kitti_dataset.py` 取逆后把相机系标注转为 LiDAR 系。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲只讲了「坐标怎么转」，还没有剖析承载 7 参数的容器本身。下一讲 [u2-l2-base-instance-3d-boxes.md](u2-l2-base-instance-3d-boxes.md) 将精读 `BaseInstance3DBoxes` 基类：`tensor` 属性、`bev` 投影、`corners` 顶点计算、`in_range_bev` 过滤以及三个子类的 yaw 约定差异。之后再进入 [u2-l3](u2-l3-point-cloud-structures.md) 的点云结构与 [u2-l4](u2-l4-det3d-data-sample.md) 的 `Det3DDataSample`，完成单元 2 的数据契约三部曲。想加深坐标直觉的读者，推荐对照阅读官方教程 [docs/en/user_guides/coord_sys_tutorial.md](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/docs/en/user_guides/coord_sys_tutorial.md) 的「Relation with raw coordinate systems of supported datasets」一节，它逐数据集说明了原始标注与本库三坐标系的关系。

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 LIDAR、CAM、DEPTH 三个坐标系各自的方向约定（哪根轴朝前、哪根轴朝上）、旋转轴与典型适用场景。
2. 使用 `Box3DMode.convert` 与 `Coord3DMode.convert` 完成 3D 框和点云的坐标系转换，并解释转换过程中坐标、尺寸、yaw 三者分别发生了什么。
3. 知道转换矩阵（如 `lidar2cam`、标定矩阵 `Rt`）在 info pkl 中的存放位置，以及数据集类在何处取用它。

本讲是单元 2（核心数据结构）的第一讲。在 [u1-l4](u1-l4-repository-structure-map.md) 中我们看到 `mmdet3d/structures` 位于星形依赖的最底层——本讲就从这个最底层中最重要的「坐标系约定」讲起。后面所有的数据集类（单元 3）、检测器（单元 4-6）、评估指标（单元 7）都建立在这套约定之上。

## 2. 前置知识

**为什么 3D 检测需要不止一套坐标系？**

在 2D 图像检测中，坐标约定几乎只有一种：原点在左上角，x 向右，y 向下。但 3D 世界里的数据来自不同物理设备，每台设备自带一套「出厂坐标」：

- **LiDAR（激光雷达）** 通常以自身旋转轴为 z 轴（朝上），前进方向为 x 轴。
- **相机** 遵循计算机视觉惯例：光轴为 z 轴（朝前），图像右方向为 x 轴，下方向为 y 轴。
- **深度相机 / RGB-D 数据**（如室内场景的 Kinect）产生的点云常用另一种约定：z 朝上，y 朝前。

此外，不同数据集与经典论文也各自「站队」：SECOND 等室外 LiDAR 方法用 LiDAR 系，VoteNet 等室内方法用 Depth 系，KITTI 原始标注却是相机系。MMDetection3D 不强行统一成一套，而是把三种约定都显式建模出来，并提供两者之间互转的工具——这就是本讲的两个主角 `Box3DMode` 与 `Coord3DMode`。

**回顾：7 自由度 3D 框。** 在 [u1-l3](u1-l3-first-inference-demo.md) 中我们已经见过，一个 3D 框由 7 个数描述：

\[
(x,\ y,\ z,\ dx,\ dy,\ dz,\ r)
\]

- \((x, y, z)\)：框的底部中心（bottom center）坐标；
- \((dx, dy, dz)\)：框沿三个坐标轴方向的边长（尺寸）；
- \(r\)：yaw 角（偏航角），即框在水平面内的朝向。

注意：这 7 个数的「含义」依赖坐标系——同样是 \(dx\)，在 LiDAR 系里是沿「前方」的边长，在相机系里是沿「右方」的边长。所以坐标系转换必须同时处理坐标、尺寸、yaw 三个量，缺一不可。

**yaw 的统一定义。** MMDetection3D 中三个坐标系都是右手系。取重力轴（LiDAR/DEPTH 的 z 轴、CAM 的 y 轴），在其垂直平面 \(\Pi\) 上取 x 轴正方向为参考方向（yaw = 0），yaw 角随方向逆时针（从重力轴负方向望向原点时）递增。一个框 yaw = 0 意味着它的「朝向边 \(dx\)」与 x 轴平行。官方文档用一句口诀概括：**框的朝向永远与 \(dx\) 边平行**。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 三大坐标系的方向约定

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

三个坐标系的方向图直接写在 `Box3DMode` 的类文档字符串里，这是全库最权威的定义处：

- **LIDAR**：z 朝上，x 朝前，y 朝左。用于 KITTI/nuScenes/Waymo 等 LiDAR 数据与 SECOND、PointPillars、CenterPoint 等室外算法。
- **CAM**：x 朝右，y 朝下，z 朝前。用于单目 3D 检测（FCOS3D、SMOKE）与 KITTI 原始标注。
- **DEPTH**：z 朝上，y 朝前，x 朝右。用于 ScanNet、SUN RGB-D 等室内数据与 VoteNet、H3DNet 等室内算法。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

把三个坐标系的关键差异整理成一张对照表：

| | LIDAR | CAM | DEPTH |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 上 | z | —（y 朝下） | z |
| 前 | x | z | y |
| 右/左 | y 朝左 | x 朝右 | x 朝右 |
| 重力轴（yaw 旋转轴） | z（axis=2） | y（axis=1） | z（axis=2） |
| 框底部中心的相对坐标 | (0.5, 0.5, 0) | (0.5, 1.0, 0.5) | (0.5, 0.5, 0) |
| 典型场景 | 室外 LiDAR 检测 | 单目 3D / KITTI 原始标注 | 室内点云检测 |

「底部中心的相对坐标」指框内一点在框自身归一化坐标系里的位置：LiDAR/DEPTH 框的 \((x,y,z)\) 指底部面中心（z 在框的最低面），而 CAM 框因 y 朝下，\((x,y,z)\) 指的是几何中心。这解释了为什么 CAM 的相对坐标是 (0.5, 1.0, 0.5)——沿 y 方向覆盖整个高度。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：在 LiDAR 坐标系中，一辆车头指向 -y 轴（正左方）的车，yaw 是多少？

**答案**：\(+\frac{\pi}{2}\)。LiDAR 系 z 朝上，从上方（z 轴负方向）俯视，x 前 y 左是逆时针方向，yaw 逆时针为正；从 x 正方向逆时针转 90° 正好指向 y 正方向（左）。源码文档 [box_3d_mode.py:L24](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L24) 的图里明确标注了 `(yaw=0.5*pi) left y`。

**练习 2**：为什么 CAM 坐标系的 yaw 旋转轴是 axis=1（y 轴），而 LIDAR 是 axis=2（z 轴）？

**答案**：yaw 定义为绕「重力轴」的旋转。LiDAR 与 DEPTH 系中 z 轴朝上（重力轴），是第 3 个分量（索引 2）；CAM 系中 y 轴朝下指向地面，重力轴是第 2 个分量（索引 1）。见 [box_3d_mode.py:L30-L31](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L30-L31) 与 [L46-L47](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/box_3d_mode.py#L46-L47)。

### 4.2 Box3DMode：框坐标系转换的引擎

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`Box3DMode.convert` 是一个静态方法，负责把任意 `src` 模式的 3D 框转换到 `dst` 模式。它解决的核心问题是：**同一个物理框，在不同坐标系下，7 个参数要同时重写**。它接受四种输入（tuple/list、numpy 数组、Tensor、`BaseInstance3DBoxes` 实例），返回同类型的结果——如果你传入的是 `LiDARInstance3DBoxes`，它会返回 `CameraInstance3DBoxes` 等目标坐标系对应的子类。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

转换分三步（以 LIDAR → CAM 为例）：

```text
输入 (x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, r)  @ LiDAR
  │
  ├─ ① 中心坐标：乘旋转矩阵 rt_mat（默认 [[0,-1,0],[0,0,-1],[1,0,0]]）
  │      x_cam = -y_lidar,  y_cam = -z_lidar,  z_cam = x_lidar
  │      等价写法：x_L = z_C, y_L = -x_C, z_L = -y_C
  │
  ├─ ② 尺寸重排：(dx, dy, dz) → (dx, dz, dy)     # y、z 互换
  │      因为 LiDAR 的 dz（高度）对应 CAM 的 dy（深度方向边长）
  │
  └─ ③ yaw 变换：r_cam = -r_lidar - π/2，再 limit_period 到 [-π, π)
  │
输出 (x', y', z', dx', dy', dz', r')  @ CAM
```

六个转换方向中 yaw 的变换公式汇总：

| 方向 | yaw 公式 | 尺寸重排 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LIDAR → CAM | \(r' = -r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| CAM → LIDAR | \(r' = -r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| DEPTH → CAM | \(r' = -r\)（纯符号翻转） | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| CAM → DEPTH | \(r' = -r\)（纯符号翻转） | \((dx, dz, dy)\) |
| LIDAR → DEPTH | \(r' = r + \frac{\pi}{2}\) | 不变 \((dx, dy, dz)\) |
| DEPTH → LIDAR | \(r' = r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) | 不变 \((dx, dy, dz)\) |

`limit_period` 的数学定义：把值限制在 \([-offset \times period,\ (1-offset) \times period)\) 内，转换中用 `period=2π`，即把 yaw 归一化到 \([-π, π)\)。计算方式为：

\[
limited\_val = val - \lfloor val / period + offset \rfloor \times period
\]

之所以出现 \(-r - \frac{\pi}{2}\) 这样的公式，是因为两个坐标系的参考方向与旋转正方向都不同：先取负号修正「逆时针/顺时针」的差异，再平移 \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) 修正「x 前方 vs x 右方」的参考方向差异。
